newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends up 14 cents, driven by US gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends up 14 cents, driven by US gasoline.

text.p: IPE October Brent futures ended up 14 cents a barrel at $19.07 on Tuesday due to soaring United States gasoline futures and a blockage to Venezuela's main oil export route.
"Gasoline was soaring. Brent got a tow higher but it slipped slightly at the end," said a floor broker.
Dealers expect a bullish report from the American Petroleum Institute later on Tuesday showing falling stocks in the U.S. for the eighth consecutive week.
NYMEX gasoline was up around two cents a gallon or 84 cents a barrel, helping to lift crude on both sides of the Atlantic.
Brent futures were also boosted by news from shipping sources that Venezuela's main oil shipping channel had been blocked.
A dredger went aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane shutting the channel to oil tankers which normally export more than one million barrels of crude per day.
Tugs were trying to refloat the dredger at 2000 Gmt on Tuesday.
Despite the strong gains on Brent futures, October was rejected by technical resistance at $19.29, the high from last Thursday.
But some dealers expect a renewed assault on that level soon if gasoline stays strong.
A few hours earlier gas oil futures ended up $2.25 a tonne at $172 for September. But a sluggish demand and brimming oil tanks were making gains difficult, said dealers.
Stocks of winter heating oil are well above year ago levels and sellers are having to work harder than buyers to drum up interest.
Prompt Rotterdam barges are at parity to the IPE, as are cargoes of Russian gas oil heading for Western buyers.
